did_you_know.text: Did you know? Daniel’s vision in chapter 8 took place in the third year of the reign of Belshazzar, king of Babylon.
Did you know? Daniel saw the vision in Susa the citadel, in the province of Elam, beside the Ulai River.
Did you know? The ram in the vision had two horns, but one was higher than the other and came up later.
Did you know? The goat came from the west with such great speed that it seemed not to touch the ground, and it had one prominent horn between its eyes.
Did you know? After the goat’s large horn was broken, four horns grew in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.
Did you know? From one of the four horns grew a small horn, which grew increasingly powerful toward the Beautiful Land, the east, and the south.
Did you know? The vision describes how the horn attacks the daily sacrifice, the sanctuary, and the truth, even throwing truth to the ground.
Did you know? In response to the question of how long the vision would last, the answer was 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary would be restored to its rightful state.
Did you know? The angel explains that the two-horned ram represents the kings of Media and Persia, while the goat represents the king of Greece.
Did you know? After seeing the vision, Daniel grew weak and was ill for several days. Then he got up, returned to the king’s service, and remained deeply troubled by the meaning of the vision.
